title: feat: route dialogue through speech API
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes `eleven-dialogue` and its aliases through `POST /v1/audio/speech` with the OpenAI-compatible string `input` field.
- Parses one `<voice>: <text>` turn per non-empty line and translates preset names or ElevenLabs voice IDs to the existing `eleven_v3` dialogue provider call.
- Removes the custom `/v1/audio/dialogue` request schema and route.
- Documents the dialogue input format and keeps the existing 10-voice, 2,000-character, usage, and billing behavior.
- Tests exact upstream translation, invalid line formatting, input limits, and generation-route coordination.

gist.headline: Dialogue finds its voice
gist.blurb: Dialogue generation has moved into the regular speech endpoint, where it can live among the other sounds without needing its own little API shed. Give each line a voice and some text; the hive handles the casting.
gist.summary: `eleven-dialogue` and its aliases now run through the OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/speech` endpoint using the string `input` field, with one `<voice>: <text>` turn per non-empty line translated to the existing `eleven_v3` dialogue provider.
gist.impact: Developers can generate up to 10-voice, 2,000-character ElevenLabs dialogue through the standard speech API while retaining existing usage and billing behavior.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy recording garden where a single retro speech terminal turns neatly formatted dialogue lines into separate glowing voice flowers. Polli, wearing tiny studio headphones, acts as the observant sound engineer beside the terminal; the monitor robot can eagerly watch the dialogue lines become audio waveforms, while vines and code-plants tie the API routing change to the garden.
